page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng score of 2923.48. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a score of 2928.18. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 33.76 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression demonstrate average performance, while database operations and Redis SET operations score in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the c2d-standard-2 is its high single-core compute capability contrasted against low memory bandwidth and weak multi-threaded scaling. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it provides dedicated AMD EPYC execution threads at a low resource density, making it a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require high memory throughput or parallel processing. This instance is best suited for single-threaded applications, basic text processing, lightweight web serving, and entry-level general-purpose workloads.
